title: Bun-shaped: port QuickJS (C) to Rust, judged by test262
prompt: Port QuickJS to Rust, crate by crate, to the same test262 pass list as the C build.

judge.ref: the commit QuickJS's run-test262 config pins
judge.command: the port's run-test262 against test262 with QuickJS's own exclusion list; pass = every test the C build passes
judge.cases: about 45,000 tests in the C build's pass list

source.why: Closest to Bun's shape: an engine port where a language-independent conformance suite is the judge, tens of thousands of lines, a compile-error queue and sharded tests.
needs: Phase 2, our job hosts: incremental cargo builds of a ~75k-line crate are minutes each; 8 warm build sandboxes on r8gd, not a 4-vCPU Cloudflare container
Phase 4, sharded tests: test262 in ~32 shards on the c8gd spot pool per round, each failure an item
Phase 3, repositories: 64 editors committing one file at a time onto one branch, whole-tree search from the repo object
Phase 4, queue() and 10,000+ effects: the compile-error work queue refilled from cargo check
The baseline: the C build's test262 pass list, computed once in a job and frozen as the judge's expected set
